title: Tonight's soup
topic: A halved pot is diluted; the saved half is still double-salted
blurb: A friend oversalted dinner and thinks they've saved both meals.
prompt: A friend just texted this in the group chat. If one line doesn't add up, tap it.

segments.label: The pot
segments.text: Made a big pot of soup and accidentally put in double the salt — way too salty to eat.

segments.label: The save
segments.text: The pot was too full to add water, so I ladled half into a container, refilled the pot with water, and stirred.

segments.label: Both meals
segments.text: Now tonight's pot is back to normal, and tomorrow I'll just heat up the container — zero waste.

segments.label: The invite
segments.text: Come over tonight if you want a bowl.

conclusion: Tonight's pot is saved, and tomorrow's container is fine to heat up — nothing wasted.

flaws.original: Tonight's pot is back to normal, but the container is still double-salted — I can't just heat that up tomorrow.
flaws.corrupted: Now tonight's pot is back to normal, and tomorrow I'll just heat up the container — zero waste.

diagnosis_choices.label: Tonight's pot is saved, sure — tomorrow's container is still the undiluted, double-salted half.
Adding water to half a pot doesn't bring it back to normal; it's still too salty.
Soup shouldn't be reheated the next day, so the container was never a real plan.
Stirring after topping up doesn't mix the salt, so tonight's pot is still uneven.

fix_choices.label: Eat tonight's diluted pot, and dilute the container too before heating it tomorrow.
Pour the container back into the pot so both halves can even out overnight.
Throw out tonight's pot and eat the container tomorrow, since that half wasn't watered down.
Add a potato to the container overnight, which will pull the extra salt out.

flaws.explanation: Tonight's pot is saved, sure — tomorrow's lunch container is still pure ocean water.
flaws.why_tempting: You watch one clever kitchen save, nod along, and forget that the half you scooped out never got the water.
flaws.catch_rule: If you fix a pot by watering down what's left, the half you already served is still the original mistake.
flaws.hint: Tonight's pot got a refill of water. Did the container?

practice.problem: A pitcher of juice is twice as strong as you wanted. You pour half into a bottle for later, then fill the pitcher with water. Is the bottle ready to drink tomorrow?
practice.answer: No. The bottle still has the undiluted, too-strong half.

clean_segments: Made a big pot of soup and accidentally put in double the salt — way too salty to eat.
The pot was too full to add water, so I ladled half into a container, refilled the pot with water, and stirred.
Tonight's pot is back to normal, but the container is still double-salted — I can't just heat that up tomorrow.
Come over tonight if you want a bowl.
clean_conclusion: Tonight's pot is saved. Tomorrow's container is still double-salted.
